# MIGRATION SPEC — MCP Python SDK v1 → v2

(As given verbatim to each Target B detection agent on 2026-08-18. The
original session's spec text was never persisted anywhere on disk, so this
is a recons

facts.text: The module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` is removed entirely in v2. Everything that lived there moves to `mcp.server.mcpserver`. Any `from mcp.server.fastmcp import X` or `import mcp.server.fastmcp` must become `from mcp.server.mcpserver import X` (respectively the `mcp.server.mcpserver` path).

The main server class `FastMCP` is renamed to `MCPServer`. `FastMCP` no longer exists under that name anywhere in the package. Every import of it, use as a type annotation, subclassing of it, or construction (`FastMCP(...)`) must have the identifier itself changed to `MCPServer` — this is a genuine class rename, not merely a change of import location.

The `Context` class moves with the rest of the module: `from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context` becomes `from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context`. `Context` KEEPS its own name — the identifier `Context` is not renamed. Nothing else about `Context` changes: its methods, its behavior, and its use as a type annotation elsewhere are all unaffected.

On the MCP client side, tool metadata objects returned by the SDK change field-naming convention from camelCase to snake_case. Specifically, `tool.inputSchema` is renamed to `tool.input_schema`; client code reading `.inputSchema` off a discovered tool object must change.
`ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()` (the class managing calls across a group of client sessions) has a changed calling contract in v2 and must be updated.
Plain `ClientSession.call_tool()` (a single session) is UNCHANGED in v2 — it must not be conflated with `ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()` and must not be flagged.

Internally, the SDK's own HTTP transport dependency changed from the `httpx` package to `httpx2`. This is purely internal to the SDK's implementation and has zero relevance to application code that imports and uses the separate `httpx` package for its own unrelated purposes (e.g. its own HTTP calls). Ordinary application-level `httpx` usage must not be flagged.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: the `@mcp.tool()`, `@mcp.resource()`, and `@mcp.prompt()` decorators have identical signature and behavior in v2.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `.add_tool(...)` is unchanged in v2.

CONFIRMED UNCHANGED (conditional): `ctx.error(...)` / `ctx.info(...)` calls that do NOT pass an `extra=` keyword argument are unchanged. Calls that DO pass `extra=` have a different, changed signature; plain calls without `extra=` are to be treated as unaffected.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `get_context()` is unchanged in v2.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: anything imported from `mcp.types` — this subpackage remains aliased and working in v2.
String literals that reference the old module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` (e.g. inside test mocks / patch targets) are also affected by the module move and must be updated to `mcp.server.mcpserver`.
Affected sites include those reached indirectly through a repo's own helper functions and test files, not just entry-point files; call chains and tests must be traced and checked.
Scope statement: the listed items are the ONLY confirmed changes in this migration — anything not described in the guide is unaffected, including things one might expect to be affected.
